use_case_title: Terminal-native autonomous coding agent for local repositories
use_case_description: A coding agent that runs as a CLI/terminal process (not an IDE plugin or web UI), directly reading and editing files, running shell commands and test suites, and committing changes in a local git repo from natural-language instructions -- letting developers stay in their existing terminal/editor/git workflow rather than adopting a new IDE.
target_users: Individual developers; software engineering and DevOps teams
business_value_rationale: Multiple independently built terminal-native agents (Aider, OpenAI Codex CLI, Warp, Cline) have shipped and gained adoption since 2023-2024, with Aider itself rated mainstream and reported time/cost savings; the shape is now a default entry point for agentic coding rather than a novel pattern.
roi_drivers: time saved; cost reduction; quality improvement

use_case_description: Turning a written specification (a PRD, issue, or design doc) into a working implementation plan and code changes: the agent decomposes the spec into tasks, scaffolds the necessary files, and iterates against the spec rather than a single ad hoc prompt, so specification quality -- not prompt engineering -- becomes the main lever on output quality.
business_value_rationale: Two independently built products (GitHub Copilot Workspace, Amazon's Kiro) have converged on the same spec-first agent workflow, and Kiro shipped in 2026 explicitly as a spec-driven successor to Amazon Q Developer -- but adoption evidence is still limited to vendor claims and early press coverage.

use_case_description: An agent delegated a full engineering task (a feature, bug fix, or app) rather than a single edit, which independently plans, writes, tests, and iterates on the implementation across multiple files/steps with minimal human intervention until it produces a working result -- as opposed to an in-editor autocomplete/pairing assistant.
target_users: Engineering teams delegating full tasks; non-engineers building internal tools
business_value_rationale: Four independently built products (Devin, Devin Desktop, Factory, Replit Agent) implement full-task delegation, with named enterprise adopters (Nubank for Devin; Adyen, Blackstone, and Groq for Factory) and Replit Agent rated mainstream for app generation -- but reliability on complex/ambiguous tasks is still inconsistent enough to classify the pattern overall as emerging.

use_case_title: Multi-agent orchestration framework for building custom production agents
use_case_description: A developer-facing SDK/framework (rather than a packaged product) for composing multiple LLM-driven agents/roles into a stateful workflow -- defining how agents hand off tasks, share memory, and call tools -- so engineering teams can build bespoke production agents on top of a foundation model instead of using a single-agent chat wrapper.
target_users: Platform/AI engineering teams; enterprise engineering teams
business_value_rationale: Three independently maintained frameworks (LangChain/LangGraph, AutoGen, Claude Agent SDK) implement the same composable multi-agent orchestration shape, with LangGraph reporting a named enterprise adopter (LinkedIn) -- but most reported production usage is still described as emerging/experimental rather than at scale.

use_case_title: Automated large-scale code migration and refactor
use_case_description: An agent pointed at a large, existing codebase and a migration/refactor goal (framework upgrade, language port, dependency bump) that autonomously plans and executes the change across many files/commits, running the test suite between steps -- distinct from single-function refactor suggestions.
business_value_rationale: Two independently built agents (Claude Code, Factory) offer a dedicated large-scale migration/refactor mode with vendor-reported internal use, addressing a widely cited pain point (technical debt/legacy maintenance consumes a large share of engineering time per industry surveys) -- but public case-study evidence beyond vendor claims is still thin.

use_case_title: AI-assisted onboarding to unfamiliar or legacy codebases
use_case_description: An agent used specifically to help a developer (new hire, or an existing engineer inheriting a legacy system) understand an unfamiliar codebase -- answering questions about how code works, tracing execution paths, and surfacing undocumented context -- rather than writing new code, shortening the ramp-up period before someone can contribute safely.
target_users: New hires; engineering teams with legacy systems
business_value_rationale: Two independently built agents (Cursor, Devin) offer onboarding/comprehension as a distinct use case with knowledge-capture framed as the value driver, addressing a recognized cost center (ramp-up time on undocumented legacy code) -- evidence is still vendor-reported rather than independently measured.
